title: Getting started with bayespk
text: Structures "1cmt" "2cmt"; routes "iv" (bolus infusion, RATE column) "oral". Covariates formulas: (WT / 70)^0.75 fixes exponent; (WT / 70)^b_wt estimates parameter named b_wt.
code: library(bayespk) mod <- pk_model("1cmt", route = "oral", iiv = c("CL", "V", "KA"), error = "proportional") mod #> bayespk model: 1cmt oral  #>   parameters: CL, V, KA  #>   between-subject variability (log-normal): CL, V, KA   #>   residual error: proportional pk_model("2cmt", route = "oral", iiv = c("CL", "V1", "KA"),          covariates = list(CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75, V1 ~ (WT / 70)^b_wt)) #> bayespk model: 2cmt oral  #>   parameters: CL, V1, Q, V2, KA  #>   between-subject variability (log-normal): CL, V1, KA   #>   residual error: proportional  #>   covariates: #>     CL ~ (WT/70)^0.75  #>     V1 ~ (WT/70)^b_wt

title: Bayesian Population Pharmacokinetics Without Writing Stan
text: Bayesian population pharmacokinetics R without writing Stan. Describe model one line, pass NONMEM-style data set , get posterior summaries, convergence diagnostics predictions new regimens. Stan programs precompiled use closed-form solutions, nothing compile fit model. Status: 0.1.0, first release. CRAN. Validated summarised ; known limitations listed inst/validation/README.md.
code: library(bayespk)  d <- nlmixr2data::theo_sd   # 12 subjects, oral theophylline  mod <- pk_model("1cmt", route = "oral", iiv = c("CL", "V", "KA"), error = "proportional") fit <- bpk_fit(mod, d, chains = 4, cores = 4)  summary(fit)                                        # posterior summaries and diagnostics predict(fit)                                        # individual predictions at observed times predict(fit, regimen = dose_regimen(320, ii = 12, n = 3))   # a new regimen

title: Bayesian Population Pharmacokinetics Without Writing Stan
text: Models: linear 1- 2-compartment; IV bolus, zero-order infusion (RATE) first-order oral absorption. Parameters CL, V (CL, V1, Q, V2) KA. oral dosing parameters apparent values (divided bioavailability). Variability: log-normal -subject variability parameter, optionally correlated. Covariates: written formulas, example CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75 (fixed exponent), CL ~ (WT / 70)^b_wt (estimated), CL ~ exp(b_age * (AGE - 40)), CL ~ (SEX == 1)^b_sex. Residual error: additive, proportional, combined, additive log scale. Priors: pk_priors(CL = lognormal(log(5), 0.5), b_wt = normal(0.75, 0.2), omega = half_normal(0.5)). Anything given gets weakly informative default, printed stored fit. Flip-flop: oral models, ka_faster = TRUE constrains typical KA disposition rate absorption known faster distribution (default). Diagnostics default: divergent transitions, tree depth, E-BFMI, R-hat effective sample sizes, check chains settle different modes, warnings. prior_sensitivity() runs power-scaling sensitivity (priorsense). version: user-written ODE models, Michaelis–Menten target-mediated elimination, steady-state records, -quantification data, inter-occasion variability, time-varying covariates pharmacodynamics.

title: Bayesian Population Pharmacokinetics Without Writing Stan
text: Scripts inst/validation; results known limitations inst/validation/README.md. Summary 2026-11-17: Closed-form concentrations agree rxode2 ODE solutions (relative error < 1e-8, including KA equal disposition rate). Simulation-based calibration: 1-cmt oral (200 replicates), 1-cmt oral estimated weight exponent (200) 2-cmt infusion (100). rank-uniformity test significant correction number parameters. Public data: theophylline warfarin (nlmixr2data). Posterior medians typical values within 1–10% nlmixr2 FOCEI estimates. 2-cmt oral simulations (40 subjects, 20 replicates): 90% interval coverage 0.85–0.95. Fits take 15 minutes one core. See vignette("bayespk") walk-. package check passed Windows R 4.5.3. 2-compartment oral simulation, 4 40 fits zero divergences maximum population R-hat 1.01. Inspect summary(fit) parameters poor mixing, use bpk_diagnostics(fit) check divergences interpreting predictions.

title: Define a population pharmacokinetic model — pk_model
text: structure "1cmt" "2cmt". route "iv" (bolus, infusion data RATE > 0) "oral" (first-order absorption). iiv Character vector parameters log-normal -subject variability. error Residual error: "additive", "proportional", "combined" "log" (additive log scale; DV must positive). covariates list formulas, one per parameter, CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75 (fixed exponent), CL ~ (WT / 70)^b_wt (estimated exponent named b_wt), CL ~ exp(b_age * (AGE - 40)) (estimated) CL ~ (SEX == 1)^b_sex (estimated effect category). Terms can multiplied: CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75 * (CRCL / 100)^b_crcl. correlated Logical; estimate correlations random effects. ka_faster Logical, oral models . TRUE, typical KA constrained larger typical disposition rate (k = CL/V 1-cmt, fast rate alpha 2-cmt) subject covariate reference values. removes flip-flop mode KA disposition rate swap. Use absorption known faster distribution; wrong flip-flop drugs many extended-release forms. prior density KA kept set zero KA <= rate (renormalised). Default FALSE.

title: bayespk 0.1.0
text: First release: 1- 2-compartment linear models (IV bolus, infusion, first-order oral), closed-form solutions, log-normal -subject variability (optionally correlated), covariate formulas, four residual error models, weakly informative default priors, diagnostics warnings, predictions new regimens, prior sensitivity. pk_model(ka_faster = TRUE) constrains typical KA disposition rate remove flip-flop modes (default). Random effects sampled sample mean plus Helmert deviations, removes correlation typical values mean random effect.
